claims.claim_text: The F-35 program is Lockheed Martin's largest program, generating ~27% of consolidated net sales in 2021 (28% 2020, 27% 2019) and 68% of Aeronautics segment net sales; production is expected to continue 'for many years' with U.S. inventory objective of 2,456 aircraft and delivery of 156 aircraft per year anticipated in 2023 and beyond.
claims.subject: Lockheed Martin
claims.object_value: F-35 Lightning II (~27% of consolidated net sales; 230 aircraft backlog into 2023)
claims.source_quote: The F-35 program is our largest program, generating 27% of our total consolidated net sales, as well as 68% of Aeronautics net sales in 2021. ... We anticipate delivering 148-153 aircraft in 2022. In 2023 and beyond, we anticipate delivering 156 aircraft for the foreseeable future. We have 230 aircraft in backlog as of December 31, 2021 extending into 2023.

claims.claim_text: Aeronautics provides modernization and sustainment activities for the U.S. Air Force's F-22 Raptor fleet, including upgrading systems requirements, adding capabilities, training systems, maintenance and integration services.
claims.subject: Lockheed Martin Aeronautics
claims.source_quote: Aeronautics continues to provide modernization and sustainment activities for the U.S. Air Force's F-22 aircraft fleet. The modernization program comprises upgrading existing systems requirements, developing new systems requirements, adding capabilities and enhancing the performance of the weapon systems.

claims.claim_text: RMS performs integrated warfare systems and sensors programs including the Aegis Combat System, which serves as an air and missile defense system for the U.S. Navy and international customers and is also a sea- and land-based element of the U.S. missile defense system (Aegis BMD).
claims.subject: Lockheed Martin RMS
claims.object_value: Aegis Combat System / Aegis Ballistic Missile Defense
claims.source_quote: Integrated warfare systems and sensors (IWSS) programs such as Aegis Combat System (Aegis) programs that serve as an air and missile defense system for the U.S. Navy and international customers and is also a sea and land-based element of the U.S. missile defense system.

claims.claim_text: Space segment major programs include Space Based Infrared System (SBIRS) and Next Generation Overhead Persistent Infrared (Next Gen OPIR), providing the U.S. Air Force with enhanced worldwide missile warning capabilities.
claims.subject: Lockheed Martin Space
claims.object_value: Next Gen OPIR-GEO and SBIRS (missile warning)
claims.source_quote: Space's major programs include: The Space Based Infrared System (SBIRS) and Next Generation Overhead Persistent Infrared (Next Gen OPIR) system programs, which provide the U.S. Air Force with enhanced worldwide missile warning capabilities.

claims.claim_text: Lockheed Martin is competing for the Next Generation Interceptor (NGI) program with the Missile Defense Agency, utilizing next generation propulsion and sensors to provide homeland missile defense.
claims.subject: Lockheed Martin
claims.source_quote: Next Generation Interceptor (NGI), a program with the MDA utilizing next generation propulsion and sensors to provide homeland missile defense.

claims.claim_text: Lockheed Martin is a primary contractor on the Long Range Discrimination Radar (LRDR) program for missile defense (named in the J-Book entity index as an LMT primary program); Aegis BMD discriminator/radar capabilities anchor a multi-year MDA pipeline.
claims.subject: Lockheed Martin
claims.source_quote: Subject notes for this cohort identify LRDR as a named LMT program (entity-index primary role).

claims.claim_text: MFC's major programs include Patriot Advanced Capability-3 (PAC-3) and Terminal High Altitude Area Defense (THAAD); higher PAC-3 volume drove $465M of MFC product sales growth in 2021. International demand from 14 nations for PAC-3 CRI/MSE.
claims.subject: Lockheed Martin MFC
claims.object_value: PAC-3 + THAAD air and missile defense systems
claims.source_quote: MFC's major programs include: The Patriot Advanced Capability-3 (PAC-3) and Terminal High Altitude Area Defense (THAAD) air and missile defense programs. ... $465 million at MFC due to higher volume on PAC-3, Long Range Anti-Ship Missile (LRASM) and Joint Air-to-Surface Standoff Missile (JASSM) programs.

claims.claim_text: Space's major programs include the Trident II D5 Fleet Ballistic Missile (FBM) — the only submarine-launched intercontinental ballistic missile currently in production in the U.S. — supporting the U.S. Navy.
claims.subject: Lockheed Martin Space
claims.object_value: Trident II D5 Fleet Ballistic Missile (FBM)
claims.source_quote: The Trident II D5 Fleet Ballistic Missile (FBM), a program with the U.S. Navy for the only submarine-launched intercontinental ballistic missile currently in production in the U.S.

claims.claim_text: Lockheed Martin claims 71% of 2021 net sales ($67.0B) from the U.S. Government (62% DoD) as a prime contractor — usaspending cross-check should confirm tens of billions of DoD obligations.
claims.subject: Lockheed Martin Corporation
claims.object_value: U.S. DoD — confirmatory cross-check on prime-contractor status
claims.source_quote: In 2021, 71% of our $67.0 billion in net sales were from the U.S. Government, either as a prime contractor or as a subcontractor (including 62% from the Department of Defense (DoD)).

claims.claim_text: Pending acquisition of Aerojet Rocketdyne for $51/share (post-dividend equity value ~$4.6B); FTC has signaled likelihood of suing to block by Jan 27, 2022 — cannot resolve via consent order. Lockheed may terminate the merger if FTC sues. Control claim (non-J-Book): tests narrative coherence around portfolio-shaping.
claims.subject: Lockheed Martin
claims.source_quote: We have been advised by the FTC that its concerns regarding the transaction cannot be addressed adequately by the terms of a consent order. We believe it is highly likely that the FTC will vote to sue to block the transaction and expect they will make a decision before January 27, 2022.

claims.claim_text: Lockheed Martin routinely applies for and owns a substantial number of U.S. and foreign patents and trademarks related to its products and services (control non-J-Book claim).
claims.subject: Lockheed Martin Corporation
claims.source_quote: We routinely apply for and own a substantial number of U.S. and foreign patents and trademarks related to the products and services we develop.
